title: Generators and yield
summary: Lazy sequences: Python's IEnumerable and yield return.

steps.title: yield
body: A function containing `yield` is a **generator**. Calling it does not run the body; it returns an iterator that runs the body a bit at a time, pausing at each `yield`. It is exactly C#'s `yield return`:

steps.explain: Nothing in the body runs until the first `next`. Each `next` runs to the following `yield`. `end` never prints because nobody asked for a third value.

steps.title: Laziness
body: Generators produce values **on demand**, so they can be infinite or huge without using memory:
A **generator expression** is the comprehension version: `(n * n for n in range(10**9))` costs nothing until you iterate. `sum(x * x for x in nums)` never builds a list.
A generator can be consumed **once**. A second loop over the same generator gets nothing.

code: squares = (n * n for n in range(4))
steps.explain: The first `sum` uses up the generator. The second finds it empty and returns 0.

steps.prompt: Why prefer `sum(len(line) for line in lines)` over `sum([len(line) for line in lines])`?
options: It never builds the intermediate list
It is the only one that works
steps.explain: Both give the same result, but the generator feeds values straight into `sum` one at a time.

steps.title: yield from and pipelines
body: `yield from other` yields everything another iterable produces. Small generators chain into pipelines, like LINQ operators:
yield from (n for n in nums if n % 2 == 0)
Each value flows through the whole pipeline before the next is read, the same streaming you get from `Where` and `Select`.

steps.prompt: Complete the generator that yields the running totals of a list.

steps.title: Fibonacci generator
prompt: Write a generator `fib()` that yields the Fibonacci numbers forever: 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, ...
Then write `take(n, iterable)` that returns a **list** of the first `n` items of any iterable (use `next` or `itertools.islice`).
template: Dojo.eq("take works on any iterable", ["a", "b"], take(2, "abc"))
Dojo.eq("take more than there are", [1, 2], take(5, [1, 2]))
Dojo.check("fib() is a generator", isinstance(fib(), types.GeneratorType), "use yield inside fib")
hints: `a, b = b, a + b` inside a `while True:` loop.
`itertools.islice(iterable, n)` takes the first n lazily.

steps.title: Chunked
prompt: Write a generator `chunks(items, size)` that yields lists of `size` consecutive items; the last chunk may be shorter. It must work on **any iterable**, including another generator, so do not use `len` or slicing on `items`.
Raise `ValueError` if `size < 1` (raising happens on first use, that is fine).
solution: raise ValueError("size must be at least 1")
template: Dojo.eq("pairs with a short tail", [[1, 2], [3, 4], [5]], list(chunks([1, 2, 3, 4, 5], 2)))
Dojo.eq("works on a generator", [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4]], list(chunks((n for n in range(5)), 3)))
Dojo.throws("size 0 raises ValueError", ValueError, lambda: list(chunks([1], 0)))
hints: Collect items into `batch`; when it reaches `size`, yield it and start a new one.
After the loop, yield what is left if it is not empty.
